newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congratulates East Timorese on Nobel award.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congratulates East Timorese on Nobel award.

text.p: The United States on Friday congratulated two East Timor independence campaigners awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize and said it hoped the award would help efforts to settle problems in the Indonesian-ruled territory.

"We congratulate these two men on winning this award," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "We hope that the action of conferring the award on them will lead to a resolution of the problems of East Timor in which the United States does have an interest."

The Norwegian Nobel Committee gave the award to Bishop Carlos Belo and resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, saying it was aimed at influencing the conflict which has festered since Indonesia invaded the territory in 1975.
At a regular State Department news conference, Burns said the United States had expressed concern in the past over human rights conditions in East Timor and would continue to do so.

But he said Washington was going ahead with a deal to sell Indonesia nine F-16 fighter planes, saying Washington has a "multifaceted" relationship with Jakarta and "will continue to have a very active and we hope positive relationship with ernment."

"We have spoken out publicly about human rights abuses in East Timor and will continue to do so," Burns said, adding that Secretary of State Warren Christopher had made the U.S. case during a visit to Jakarta last summer.
